turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he had any other residences to his name, for a gentleman of his position ought to have more than one establishment.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack explained that his other residence was in the country, a small place called Woolton, where he had a great many friends, though he admitted he had not yet called on them as he had only recently arrived there.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen rolled her eyes at her mother’s questioning, telling her, in a reproachful tone, that she wished they could discuss more important matters than Jack’s residences.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell raised an eyebrow at Jack’s explanation, her voice taking on a tone of disapproval. She told him, in a cutting manner, that while a country residence might be charming, it was imperative for a gentleman to have a presence in London if he wished to marry into a family of her standing.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded, acknowledging Lady Bracknell’s criticism, and told her, somewhat hesitantly, that he understood her concerns and would be happy to establish a more prominent presence in London if that was necessary to please her and win Gwendolen’s hand.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She fixed her gaze on Jack, her tone unwaveringly critical, as she informed him that understanding her concerns was not enough; a man must demonstrate a commitment to upholding the standards of his class and society.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood the gravity of Lady Bracknell’s words, he told her, and he was committed to doing everything in his power to live up to the expectations of his future role in society.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She fixed her gaze upon Jack, her tone unyielding, as she informed him that mere words of commitment meant little; actions were what truly mattered in the circles in which they moved.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood the importance of actions, he told Lady Bracknell, and promised to demonstrate his commitment through deeds rather than just words.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She fixed her eyes upon Jack, her tone icy, as she informed him that promises of action were a start, but she would wait to see tangible results before considering his suitability.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack was determined to meet Lady Bracknell’s expectations, he told her, and would work diligently to prove his worth.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She would wait to see tangible results before making any judgments, she informed Jack, and expected him to provide evidence of his worthiness through his actions and not just his words.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell that she was engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she was not engaged to anyone and that when she did become engaged, she or her father would inform her of the fact.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell, 'Mamma!'

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to go to the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to get into the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack to take a seat.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he preferred standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she felt bound to inform him that he was not down on her list of eligible young men.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he must admit he smoked.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was glad to hear it and that a man should always have an occupation of some kind.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he knew everything or nothing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he knew nothing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was pleased to hear it and that she did not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if his income was in land or in investments.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was in investments.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that it was satisfactory.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he had a country house with some land attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that a country house was satisfactory and asked how many bedrooms it had.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned a house in Belgrave Square, but it was let by the year to Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she did not know Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that Lady Bloxham went about very little and was a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that nowadays that was no guarantee of respectability of character and asked what number in Belgrave Square.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that the number was 149.
